a.headline: I trusted Adobe Firefly because it was the safe AI option, now I'm not so sure
a.summary: This piece interrogates the promise of Adobe Firefly as an ethically trained AI tool and raises new doubts about whether that claim holds up. If you use Firefly in your workflow, this is essential reading for understanding the limits of so-called safe generative AI.

a.headline: Reframe: David Sheldon-Hicks and Art Tindsley open a new podcast with Patrice Vermette
a.summary: Territory Studio founder David Sheldon-Hicks and Pogo launch a new podcast exploring the intersection of creativity and technology, opening with Dune production designer Patrice Vermette. For motion design students, this is a valuable window into how leading studios are navigating creative practice in the age of AI.

a.headline: The Conversation: The state of freelancing
a.summary: As agencies rethink how they hire talent and AI tools reshape production pipelines, this piece examines the shifting landscape for freelance creatives. For students about to enter the industry, understanding these structural changes is as important as building a strong portfolio.

b.headline: The Download: Pelosi's successor targets AI and data centers face power woes
b.summary: This edition of MIT Tech Review's daily newsletter covers growing political and infrastructural pressure on data centres as their power demands escalate. It is a timely reminder that every AI tool you use in a studio is tethered to an energy grid under increasing strain.

c.headline: Max Cameron roasts the arrogance of AI tech bros with subversive cigarette packaging
c.summary: Senior Mother London copywriter Max Cameron has designed a series of fake cigarette packs that mirror the health warnings on tobacco packaging, applying them directly to the wilder claims of AI hype. It is a razor-sharp piece of critical design that uses familiar visual language to puncture Silicon Valley hubris.

c.headline: AI DJs Completely Kill My Groove
c.summary: This essay critically examines how YouTube Music and Spotify have deployed synthetic AI hosts to curate playlists, arguing that their hollow banter and fabricated trivia actively degrade the listening experience. It raises important questions about what is lost when human curation and taste are replaced by generative performance.

c.headline: Georgie McAusland on refusing expensive tools to get more squish and texture into her drawings
c.summary: Illustrator Georgie McAusland deliberately avoids expensive digital tools, instead drawing on location to capture the textures and atmosphere that software tends to flatten. Her practice is a quiet but clear statement about the value of physical presence and material resistance in image-making.
